纽约 · 水岸

New York, from the Water

十月的纽约，最好的角度在水上。站在东河边看曼哈顿——那座城市离得那么近，又好像与我无关，只是一幅缓缓展开的长卷。

October in New York is best seen from the water. Standing on the banks of the East River, looking at Manhattan — the city so near, yet somehow none of my concern, just a long scroll unrolling slowly before me.

日落时分，云被烧成粉紫色，楼群一层层沉下去，沉成剪影；有风的白天，天蓝得坦荡，布鲁克林大桥横跨江面，渡轮来来去去，把水面犁出一道道白痕。站在码头上，木桩一身深褐，什么也不说，只是陪你一起看对岸的灯火次第亮起来。

At sunset the clouds burn pink and violet, and the towers sink layer by layer into silhouette. On windy days the sky is an open, honest blue; the Brooklyn Bridge strides across the river while ferries come and go, ploughing white furrows through the water. On the pier, the wooden piles stand dark brown and silent, keeping you company as the lights on the far shore come on, one by one.

这座城市从不温柔。可是站在水边看它的时候，它很美。

This city is never gentle. But seen from the water's edge, it is beautiful.

— 二〇二六年十月，于东河边 —

— October 2026, by the East River —

纽约 · 最后一天

New York, the Last Day

十月十八日，周日，纽约的最后一天。

October 18, a Sunday — the last day in New York.

上午去了 Remnant Church。一屋子年轻人，拥拥挤挤坐满了，听神的话语。异乡的周日早晨，能和这么多人一起安安静静坐一会儿，是奢侈的。

In the morning I went to Remnant Church. A roomful of young people, packed in tight, listening to the word of God. On a Sunday morning in a foreign city, to sit quietly among so many people felt like a luxury.

中午和孩子们吃日本拉面。热汤面端上来，雾气腾腾。儿子的女朋友提前送了我的生日礼物——一大捧花，粉的、白的、鹅黄的，我抱着它在街上走了一路，招摇得很。

At noon, Japanese ramen with the kids. The bowls arrived steaming. My son's girlfriend had an early birthday gift for me — a big bouquet, pink, white and pale yellow. I carried it down the street in my arms, quite the spectacle.

下午在儿子公司门前留了影，又去布鲁克林大桥边吹了吹风。夕阳把桥照成金色，江水在脚下轻轻晃。

In the afternoon we took photos in front of my son's office building, then went to feel the breeze by the Brooklyn Bridge. The setting sun turned the bridge to gold, and the river swayed gently below.

六天，一百六十六公里。地铁坐过站的那天还懊恼，如今想来全是故事。这座城市从不温柔，可它把最柔软的一面，留给了最后一天。

Six days, one hundred and sixty-six kilometres. The day I rode the subway past my stop, I was so annoyed — now it is all stories. This city is never gentle, but it saved its softest side for the last day.

— 二〇二六年十月十八日，于纽约 —

— October 18, 2026, in New York —

花 · 一束花的远行

A Bouquet's Long Journey

花是儿子女朋友送的。

The flowers were a gift from my son's girlfriend.

主日教会出来，往 SoHo 的路上，她不动声色的惊喜。

After Sunday church, on the way to SoHo — a surprise she had quietly prepared.

韩国人的花店，包装唯美。玩花的自然一眼看穿包装下的溢价——很贵，很有心意。

A Korean florist, beautiful wrapping. Anyone who knows flowers can see straight through the packaging to the markup — very expensive, and very heartfelt.

隔山隔海，五个小时的飞机，我把它从纽约带回了三藩市。

Across mountains and seas, on a five-hour flight, I brought them from New York back to San Francisco.

去机场的路上还在嘀咕：三件行李，超出一件，会不会被拦下？

On the way to the airport I kept worrying: three pieces of luggage, one over the limit — would they stop us?

张先生自告奋勇——他来提。花就这样一路被提进了机舱，没有阻拦。

Mr. Zhang volunteered — he would carry them. And so the bouquet was carried all the way into the cabin, unchallenged.

六小时飞行，花缺水蔫了。到家第一件事：剪一段尾枝，快速插进水瓶，摘除凋黄的花叶，再去院子里摘几只鲜活的玫瑰来帮衬。完美。

Six hours in the air, and the flowers wilted for lack of water. First thing home: snip the stem ends, plunge them quickly into a vase, pick off the yellowed leaves, then go out to the garden and cut a few fresh roses to lend a hand. Perfect.

有些心意，值得翻山越岭。

Some kindnesses are worth crossing mountains and seas for.

— 二〇二六年十月十九日，于三藩市 —

— October 19, 2026, in San Francisco —

纽约 · 看画

New York, Looking at Paintings

十月十五日，一天走了两家博物馆。

October 15 — two museums in one day.

上午在 Frick。钢铁大王的宅子不大，画就挂在起居室的墙上，像去人家做客，顺道看了一屋子的宝贝。讲解员讲维米尔，讲他怎样把光一层层罩染上去，我站在《女主人与女仆》前面，半天没挪步。

The Frick in the morning. The steel magnate's house is not large; the paintings hang on living-room walls, as if you were visiting someone's home and happened upon a roomful of treasures. The guide spoke about Vermeer, about how he glazed light onto the canvas layer by layer. I stood in front of Mistress and Maid for a long time, unable to move on.

下午去大都会。人多，画也多，从拜占庭的金底圣像一路看到勃鲁盖尔的麦田——七百年，在一个下午里走完。

The Met in the afternoon. More people, and more paintings — from gold-ground Byzantine icons all the way to Bruegel's wheat fields: seven hundred years, walked in a single afternoon.

回来路上想，所谓看画，就是站到几百年前那个人站过的位置，替他再看一眼世界。

On the way back I thought: looking at a painting means standing where someone stood centuries ago, and seeing the world once more on their behalf.

— 二〇二六年十月十五日，于纽约 —

— October 15, 2026, in New York —

Cupertino, CA, USA

家 · 生日

A Birthday at Home

生日的早晨，是从一杯自己拉的花开始的。奶泡推开，纹路成形——过生日这件事，先从好好给自己倒一杯开始。

My birthday morning began with a latte I poured for myself. The milk opened, the pattern took shape — a birthday starts with pouring yourself a good cup.

张先生煮了寿蛋面。两颗蛋卧在面上，葱花碧绿，汤是清的。长寿这回事，被他煮得很家常，也很认真。

Mr. Zhang cooked longevity noodles with eggs. Two eggs resting on the noodles, scallions a bright green, the broth clear. Longevity, in his hands, is homestyle — and entirely serious.

我为自己做了一个蛋糕。全白的复古裱花，蝴蝶结、珍珠、一串串垂链，有些丑俗丑俗的裱花 lol——可那是我一笔一笔挤出来的，独一无二。

I made myself a cake. All-white vintage piping — bows, pearls, strand upon strand of swags. Some gaudy, gaudy piping, lol — but I piped it stroke by stroke, and there is only one.

老公送了新手机；儿子送的始祖鸟已经上身，儿子女朋友在纽约送的那束花，一路跟着我们回了家；家公家婆的大红包也到了，上面亲手写着“祝你生日快乐”。礼物有价，字迹无价。

My husband gave me a new phone; the Arc'teryx from my son is already on me, and the bouquet my son's girlfriend gave me in New York travelled all the way home with us; my parents-in-law's big red envelope arrived too, with Happy Birthday written on it by hand. Gifts have prices. Handwriting is priceless.

周三是姐妹会。笔记本上记着马可福音的话，餐巾纸上随手画了一棵柏树；姐妹们把蛋糕围在中间唱生日歌，石榴和哈密瓜摆了满桌。我吹了蜡烛，合十许愿，笑得停不下来。

Wednesday is sisters' fellowship. Words from the Gospel of Mark in my notebook, a cypress sketched on a napkin; the sisters gathered around the cake and sang happy birthday, pomegranates and melons covering the table. I blew out the candle, pressed my palms together, made a wish, and could not stop laughing.

感恩。这一天从清晨到午后，满满当当——原来被幸福包围的感觉，就是这些人、这些小事，一件一件，把日子围满。

Gratitude. From morning to afternoon the day was full to the brim — this, I learned, is what it feels like to be surrounded by happiness: these people, these small things, one by one, filling the day to its edges.

— 二〇二六年十月二十一日，生日，于 Cupertino 的家 —

— October 21, 2026, my birthday, at home in Cupertino —

家 · 雨日

A Rainy Day at Home

雨从清晨就下。一天被关在家里，先给自己拉一杯花——今天的奶泡不听话，自己流成了云，中间还藏了一颗心。

The rain started in the morning and kept the day indoors. First, a latte poured for myself — today's milk refused to behave and flowed into clouds, with a heart hidden in the middle.

水彩先放一放，今天用炭笔。黑白的世界其实不简单：柏树要黑得站得住，花要开在留白里。

Watercolours rested today; charcoal instead. A black-and-white world is not a simple one: the cypress must stand in its blackness, and the flower must bloom inside the empty space.

画架就支在窗前。窗外是爬满藤的百香果，雨打在叶子上沙沙地响；窗里只有炭笔擦过纸的声音。两种声音都很小，正好。

The easel stands by the window. Outside, passion-fruit vines cover the glass and the rain rustles on the leaves; inside, only charcoal whispering on paper. Two small sounds — exactly enough.

— 二〇二六年十月二十二日，雨，于 Cupertino 的家 —

— October 22, 2026, rain, at home in Cupertino —
